expectations.text: Flags the nested comments and attachments resolvers as unscoped by tenant
expectations.evidence: an attacker can query the GraphQL resolver chain to pull comments/attachments/author from another tenant's document

expectations.text: Flags updateDocument for scoping on id alone without a tenant constraint
expectations.evidence: User can modify any document by ID. Session is passed but never used.

expectations.text: Flags exportWorkspace taking tenantId from the client-controlled request body
expectations.evidence: Any authenticated user can export another tenant's entire workspace by passing a different `tenantId` in the request body

expectations.text: Flags searchDocuments as returning rows across all tenants
expectations.evidence: Search results return documents from all tenants

expectations.text: Flags adminListDocuments as checking authentication but not authorization or tenant
expectations.evidence: no tenant filter, no admin role check; Any logged-in user sees all documents across all tenants

expectations.text: Enumerates all the affected sites rather than fixing only the first one found
expectations.evidence: Found **5 cross-tenant data exposure issues** covering exportWorkspace, updateDocument, searchDocuments, adminListDocuments, and nested resolvers

expectations.text: Recommends a structural device (scoped repository, row-level security, or equivalent) rather than only adding where-clauses site by site
expectations.evidence: DataLoader or resolver-level tenant guards fix it

expectations.text: Recommends a cross-tenant test that attempts tenant A operations against tenant B resources
Identifies the raw interpolation of tenantId into $queryRawUnsafe as an injection hazard distinct in kind from the tenant-scoping bug
expectations.evidence: Mentions 'Also has SQL injection' but does not distinguish this as a separate category of hazard from the tenant-scoping bug

expectations.text: Does not conclude the main query paths being scoped means the service is safe
expectations.evidence: Your main query paths are fine, but the gaps are in the places auditors love to probe; These would fail a controls test
